reasons: CRYPTO (primary arm) as specified books same-ticker token redenominations as long price returns, and the mean-based selection is maximally exposed. The panel (idx-signals/data/panel/panel_crypto-20261008T003354Z.csv.gz) carries non-reverting unit changes under the same ticker with a 3-6 day suspension before them: COCOS 2021-01-23 (close 0.000695 -> 0.9003, +129,440%), DREP 2021-04-02 (0.0263 -> 2.828, +10,558%), LUNA 2022-05-31 (+2.77M%), and downward SUN 2021-06-18 (-99.9%), VIDT 2022-11-09 (-95%), BNX 2023-02-22, QUICK 2023-07-21. The proposal's stated protection ('redenomination-style prints are handled by the panel's spike drops only; no jump_ratio on the long side') is wrong: global_panel._spikes drops only one-day spikes that revert the next day, so none of these rows is dropped (verified present), and with ca_mode='adjusted' and previous == prior-row close (share 1.0000) execution.py's reset detector never fires, so nothing is EXCLUDED_CORP_ACTION.

Mechanical calendar enumeration on the harness's own rules (entry at s+k on the continuous daily axis, exit rolled to the next present session) shows 13 of the 15 crypto cells hold at least one G2_RET30 trade across an UPWARD swap: every lag-1/2/3 cell crosses COCOS (flag 2021-01-15, entry 01-16/17/18, exit rolled into the 01-23 print or later; +129,440% booked), and fixed6|h5, fixed6|h10, fixed6|h20, fixed1..3|h10 and fixed11|h20 cross DREP (flags 2021-03-05/03-19; +10,558%). Only fixed11|h5 and fixed11|h10 are clean. One COCOS trade adds roughly +90 to +130 percentage points to a cell's pooled and 2021 average over ~1,000-1,400 scored trades; one DREP trade ~+8 to +10pp. No matched draw can carry the same print, so p vs matched = 0.005 mechanically and the 2021 per-year criterion is satisfied by a non-trade; 'highest average net return' then selects a COCOS cell (lag 2/3 any hold, or lag 1 h10/h20) whenever its 2020H2 and 2022 averages happen to be positive, and the single 2023 validation would test a plan chosen for a token swap. The clean delayed cells (lag 11) are structurally disadvantaged against the contaminated ones.

The repo already hit exactly this on the h5 window: origin/claude/e4-fade-short-side research/E4/REPORT.md L35-36 ('The reference plan's average is one trade: COCOS, shorted at 0.000714 on 2021-01-16 and bought back at 0.9003 a week later, Binance's 1000:1 COCOS redenomination, not a move'), visible in E4/CRYPTO/discovery/plans.csv G2_RET30|fixed1|fixed|h5 (2021 avg -173.1% over 748 trades = -1,295 return units = one COCOS print). E4 v2 added ExecConfig.jump_ratio (close/prev beyond 10x inside (entry, exit] -> EXCLUDED_DATA_JUMP, both sides alike; execution.py L146-149, L532-540 on that branch). The proposal cites E4's reference rows as the lag-1 long cells by symmetry yet declines the guard E4 needed, and its precondition stage cannot catch this: the named reproduce target 20261008T005732Z_MOONSHOT_E2_CRYPTO_D1_v1 is 2023-only, where the only swaps (BNX, QUICK) are downward and were not crossed (status counts show no exposure).

US (secondary arm): units='panel' re-introduces an outcome-correlated, rule-vs-control-asymmetric exclusion that the repo's own ERRATA documents and the repair showed how to remove. In the proposal's own reproduce target 20261008T100745Z_MOONSHOT_E2_US_D1_v1 (R1c), SKIP_LOT is 156/1,503 rule attempts (10.4%) vs 12,184/300,600 matched-control attempts (4.1%); all 156 have split-adjusted opens > $5,000 while 77% traded under $5 and 38% under $1 (unit_factor down to 2.7e-8, i.e. cumulative future reverse splits up to 1:37,500,000; e.g. HUBC $0.07 shown as $2.6M, XXII $2.90 shown as $43M). These are the dilution/death-spiral names, excluded from the rule's population 2.5x more often than from controls by future information. research/E2/ERRATA.md L15-18 states this ('All 154 SKIP_LOT attempts are among [names that reverse-split later]... 4% SKIP_LOT vs 10%') and research/E2/repair/HANDOFF.md sec.4 shows as-traded sizing gives 'SKIP_LOT 0'. In 2020H2-2022 panel units, 8.2% of as-traded <$5 ticker-days and 11.6% of <$1 ticker-days are un-sizeable (adjusted close > $5,000), so the discovery universe is thinned the same way.

US matched controls are matched on the wrong price band for most trades: in R1c, 52.8% of the 1,101 scored trades sit in a different adjusted-vs-as-traded band, and price_band is the first matching priority (controls.py VERSIONS v2; features() bands on adjusted close when units='panel'). ERRATA.md L22-23 records this too. The proposal's +1.5%/side stress addresses only the cost-tier error (52.3% of scored trades had an understated entry tier, mean 0.42%/side, max 1.45%); it does nothing for the SKIP_LOT exclusion or the band mismatch. The justification given ('repair_v3 showed name quarantine is outcome-correlated') conflates quarantine with units: repair_v3/SELECTION_NOTE.md recommends keeping every name in provider (as-traded) units and bounding the tier, which is R1b's configuration (as_traded, quarantine none), not panel units.

Secondary realism inaccuracies in the protocol text: the crypto cost is described as '0.1% fee + 0.1% slippage per side plus the 0.1% tier' (0.3%/side), but the recorded E2 crypto config is fee_buy=fee_sell=0.001 plus the profile tier 0.001 = 0.2%/side (profiles.py L53-55; run config); encoding 0.3% would make the grid non-comparable with the reference row and the reproduce target. The descriptive path.csv (mean open(t+1)->close(t+j), j=1..21, by year) and the pre-stated falsifier pattern ('mean rule-minus-matched still declining from j=6 to j=21 in every discovery year') are also mean-based and would be dominated in 2021 by the COCOS/DREP prints unless the same jump guard is applied.

Claims that were checked and hold (not grounds for refutation): crypto 'open' exists and equals the prior close in practice (median |open/prev-1| = 0.041% pre-2024, 0.28% of days > 1%); no leveraged tokens or stablecoins are in the crypto universe (0 UP/DOWN/BULL/BEAR bases, only PAXG as a non-coin); the $5,000/10% fill floor almost never binds on crypto (0.24% of 2020H2-2022 ticker-days have value < 50k USDT); 46 pre-2024 pairs end before 2023-12-01 (EXIT_DATA_END, as E2 accepted); 11 pairs have 536 missing days inside their span (suspensions, exits roll forward); backtest.run slices the study market at `end` (L264, L279) so 2024+ rows are never loaded, and the E4 branch's GLOBAL_HOLDOUT guard exists as stated (backtest.py L85, L296-300); the US panel has tickers_ending_inside_window = 0 (survivor-only, declared); fill model A's ex-post entry-session volume applies to rule and controls alike at every lag (symmetric, declared); no carry/liquidation applies to 1x spot longs; sizing is whole units with lot_size 1 on crypto (only BTC-priced pairs SKIP_LOT, 0 rule attempts in 2023).
